title: Pair Concatenation with a Space Bound
statement: There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean word $z$, $M$ halts within $c(|z|+1)$ steps and outputs the concatenation of the two components returned by the aligned pair parser when it succeeds, and outputs the empty word when it fails. For every Boolean word $z$ and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the computation through step $t$ uses at most $c(|z|+1)$ work-tape cells.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of a finite Turing machine over Booleans
Existence of a natural-number constant c
Computes the parser-success concatenation, or the empty word on parser failure, within c(|z|+1) steps on every input
For every input and every t, space through step t is at most c(|z|+1)
